constrains.how: FGFR1 is a single-pass cell-surface receptor: three Ig-like C2-type repeats (25-119, 158-246, 255-357 aa) then a kinase (478-767 aa). The ligand-binding face is on the ectodomain, so the model's receptor readout can only be evaluated on a bounded extracellular surface, not on the full 500 um domain. It also sets a ~333 aa (~30-40 nm) ectodomain scale that must not be confused with the 25 um sigma.
constrains.model_parameter: the receptor term theta = L/(K_D + L) and sigma_um = 25 um
constrains.strength: qualitative bound on the readout population and on the validity of a free-ligand field reaching a cell-surface receptor

sources.class: parameter / measured in vivo diffusion + free-vs-bound pool partition (time series)

constrains.how: a measured in vivo FRAP dataset that explicitly separates a diffusible pool from a membrane-bound pool and quantifies their exchange. That is the same measurement that produced Harish et al.'s 93%/7% fast/slow split, so it is the closest public analogue for the slow pool the frozen model omits.
constrains.model_parameter: D_um2_per_s = 55.0 and D_slow_um2_per_s = 4.0, and the excluded 7% slow/HSPG-bound pool
constrains.strength: scale bound only, and a different compartment
constrains.why_not_stronger: Dystrophin is a sarcolemmal/cytoskeletal protein, not a secreted morphogen, and the embryo is not a 500 um 1-D domain. It cannot confirm or refute 55 or 4 um^2 s^-1 numerically.

constrains.how: tells you, quantitatively, in which cell types FGFR transcripts are present, i.e. which cell classes are eligible to be 'receptor-bearing' in the readout. Without a receptor-bearing population, x_KD = 459.52 um is a distance no cell can sample.
